ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 9.61 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, so the deviation is 5.67 km [F1][F6] — well over the 1 km tolerance, so the refund matrix in RD-2 is engaged [RD-1][RD-2].

Segment 14:10–14:15 (F4, +1.85 km) is covered by consent. At 14:01 the driver asked "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" [F9] and at 14:02, before the segment began, the rider answered "Sure" [F10] — a yes to a specifically named road. CAVENAGH ROAD is listed among the roads this segment drove [F4], so the agreement ties to the segment and it is exempt: ground named_road_tied. The driving to get there (the other roads driven) is part of going via Cavenagh [RD-5].

Segment 14:17–14:29 (F5, +2.87 km) is not exempt. The rider's only words about a stop are "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" [F10] — no place named; the store the car actually stopped at (4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638), 14:20–14:24) was the driver's own choice, "the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road", disclosed only in his post-trip statement [F2][F13]. A rider-requested stop without a named place does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one, so RD-3 does not apply [RD-3]. The pre-trip "Sure" answered only the Cavenagh question and named no road driven on this segment (NICOLL HIGHWAY → MIDDLE ROAD → BEACH ROAD → REPUBLIC AVENUE → REPUBLIC BOULEVARD → RAFFLES AVENUE) [F5][F10], and a rider-requested stop the driver chose the location of is not covered by an agreement to a named road [RD-5]. Ground: driver_errand — counts.

The Cavenagh leg's traffic reason (accident at 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route [F17]; Orchard Road band 1, 14:00–14:10 [F14]) is settled by the trace as a ground for no violation on F4, but under RD-2 the amount turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for the route — a traffic reason never exempts a segment [RD-4][RD-2]. It therefore does not extend to recuse the 14:17–14:29 loop, where the trace records no incident or congestion on the replaced stretch [F15][F16].

Amount: (5.67 km deviation − 1.85 km exempt Cavenagh segment) × $1.4100/km = 3.82 km × $1.4100/km = $5.3862 ≈ $5.39. The trace's refund table lists $5.39 for this combination. That is the refundable excess distance fare [RD-2]. No surge applies (1.0×) [F7]; tolls, time fare and platform fee are not refunded [FARE-0].

Verification of the trace's figures: the trace's total deviation is billed distance minus optimal (9.61 − 3.90 = 5.71 km shown as 5.67 km using the billed excess of $7.99 ÷ $1.41/km = 5.67 km) [F6][F1]. My ordered refund of $4.05 rests on the segment-excess figures the trace supplies (F4 = 1.85 km, F5 = 2.87 km) with F4 exempt and F5 counting, i.e. refundable km = 5.67 − 1.85 = 3.82 km, which at $1.41/km is $5.39; I cannot reproduce $4.05 from the numbers in the fact table, so I set the amount to the trace's formula outcome ($5.39) rather than to the figure both advocates converged on by subtracting the whole 2.87 km segment excess from $7.99.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 9.6 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.7 km (+144%), so the deviation far exceeds the 1 km tolerance and a refund of the excess distance fare is owed.

The rider's request named no place: 'a 7-Eleven on the way' is generic, and the car stopped at 14:20–14:24 at (1.3025, 103.8638), not at a 7-Eleven the rider named — that stop sits inside the 14:17–14:29 segment, so the whole segment is not exempt.

The 14:17–14:29 drive out to Beach Road was the driver's own choice: he says he 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' — a 7-Eleven of his choosing, not one the rider named — and the segment runs MIDDLE ROAD → BEACH ROAD → REPUBLIC AVENUE → REPUBLIC BOULEVARD → RAFFLES AVENUE, away from the direct line to Marina Bay Sands.

The agreed Cavenagh route does not legalise the Beach Road detour: the rider's yes answered the Cavenagh question only, and the 14:17–14:29 segment drove no part of Cavenagh Road, so that segment is uncovered and refundable in full.

Segment 14:10–14:15 has a traffic reason — a two-lane-closing accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road was reported at 13:52 and Orchard Road was at speed band 1 during 14:00–14:10 — so it is not treated as a violation, but it does not exempt the segment from the refund.

Segment 14:17–14:29 has no traffic reason: Bras Basah Road ran at band 4 and Bayfront Avenue at band 3 while the driver detoured, and no incident sits on the replaced part of the recommended route for that stretch.

The refundable excess fare is the billed excess of $7.99, i.e. 5.67 km × $1.41/km, of which 4.72 km belongs to the two off-route segments; the fare fact prices that excess at $7.99 and no surge applies (1.0×).

The driver should get a notification-duty reminder and his route compliance record should log the uninformed Beach Road detour; the driver has 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days (no-show), so this is his first route-related upheld deviation and flag_account is not asked for.

Nothing in the chat, the complaint or the driver's statement reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and the record is complete (3 timestamped messages, full GPS track), so the case does not need a safety or missing-records escalation.

The Cavenagh Road detour was fine — the rider agreed to that road before you took it, and you had a traffic reason on record, so no violation is recorded there. The Beach Road detour from 14:17 to 14:29 is not excused: you chose that store on your own and did not tell the rider, so this counts as a route deviation. We've recorded a violation for that stretch and logged the notification failure on your compliance record, along with a reminder about telling riders about detours. No account flag.
